questions.prompt: To create View B from View A, which SOLIDWORKS view type was inserted?

questions.prompt: To create View B from View A, which SOLIDWORKS view type was inserted?
questions.explain: A straight cutting line (A–A) drawn across the parent view, with the hatched result placed as a new view, is a Section View. An aligned section needs a bent cutting line; a broken-out section stays inside the original view; a detail view enlarges a circled region.

questions.prompt: To create View B from View A, which SOLIDWORKS view type was inserted?
questions.explain: A circle on the parent view, labelled with a letter, shown again at a larger scale as "DETAIL C" is a Detail View. A crop view hides everything outside a closed profile but keeps the scale and replaces the original view.

questions.prompt: To create View B from View A, which SOLIDWORKS view type was inserted?
questions.explain: An Auxiliary View is projected perpendicular to a selected reference edge (here the inclined edge), so the inclined face appears at its true size. A projected view only goes in the standard orthographic directions.
